records.title: Fix problems with running payroll You made a mistake in your FPS or EPS
records.locator: Opening correction list; payment-date, personal-information and EPS sections
records.point: The guidance identifies reporting errors affecting a PAYE bill and distinct correction routes, including duplicate-record risks. Correct employee payment, correct statutory reporting and correction effort are different outcomes.
records.population: Guidance for relevant UK employers or workers; not a survey
records.limitations: Operational mechanism and consequence context only. No market prevalence, automatic penalty, causal ROI or organisation-specific tax/legal advice inferred. Recheck rules at final publication.

records.title: PAYE and payroll for employers Keeping records
records.locator: Keeping records; lost stolen or destroyed records
records.point: Payroll records include payments, deductions, reports, HMRC payments and relevant supporting information. Record evidence and recoverability are separate operating needs from paying employees correctly.
records.population: Guidance for relevant UK employers or workers; not a survey
records.limitations: Operational mechanism and consequence context only. No market prevalence, automatic penalty, causal ROI or organisation-specific tax/legal advice inferred. Recheck rules at final publication.

records.title: Universal Credit and employers
records.point: Incorrect or late earnings information can affect the Universal Credit a claimant expects. Employers do not need to know which employees receive it. The reporting consequence is relevant without collecting personal benefit status.
records.population: Guidance for relevant UK employers or workers; not a survey
records.limitations: Operational mechanism and consequence context only. No market prevalence, automatic penalty, causal ROI or organisation-specific tax/legal advice inferred. Recheck rules at final publication.

records.title: Handling unpaid wages
records.point: Payroll delay or incorrect payment requires communication and correction; financial difficulty and charges are possible consequences. The guidance is not evidence of incidence, retention effects or a typical cost per error.
